title: Putting heads on his own banjo and Bunk Johnson
summary: He fixed banjo heads himself, sometimes using drum heads, and recalls Bunk driving a float and buying beer.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: How about putting a cover on? Something happened to his banjo and he didn't want to spend money to buy a new and he put a cover on it when he took it down to the place and after that he began to put the head on the banjo.

You say how about the cover, the cover you made for your banjo? The cover? The head. The head? The head, the head for your banjo. Did I have a cover? No, the head you made for it. You mean could I put them on with a bust? Yeah. You remember I.C. don't you? Yeah. And then Trumpet there. I see, you remember him, right? Yeah, I remember I see. I mean, Cyclops there. And he liked me how to put them in. And then Professor Bo Reese, he liked me.

Could you tell us about the time that you broke your banjo and you didn't want to buy a new one so you decided you'd put a head on it and cover it and fix it yourself. Oh, I used to fix it myself. You know.

When I first got it, I used to carry them, you know, where the picture was, where I bought them. Then again, the other photos, the picture, I used to carry them too. And I learned how to put them on myself. Oh, I didn't bother them. They had no trouble. I used to pay seven, eight dollars for my head. Sometimes I used to use a drum head with a bunch of drums, you know. It wasn't harmonized to it, you know.
